adversarial_audit.objection: Different cyclic subgroups can share a large coefficient sector.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Any proper intersection has zero mass at even index or inverse-square mass at odd index; Cauchy caps correlation at 1/3.

adversarial_audit.objection: Replacing u by min(u,m-u) silently changes the crossing count.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The proof bounds both positive and negative half-images for the smaller multiplier; negation swaps them exactly.

adversarial_audit.objection: Axis points invalidate the square-wave mismatch formula for even order.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Every unit fixes 0 and m/2; their two +1 contributions give the same exact identity T=m-4d.

adversarial_audit.objection: Vanishing normalized Frobenius residual gives a uniform condition number.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False. It gives only a maximally-mixed-domain tail bound; small exceptional singular sectors can remain.

adversarial_audit.objection: The theorem supplies an efficient quantum algorithm.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False. Structured access, physical input domination, decoding, and a classical separation remain open gates.

falsifiers_triggered: Pointwise finite stress is no longer used as the proof of the 3/4 ceiling.
The theorem does not imply a uniform singular-value gap.
The theorem does not identify arbitrary physical input mass with the maximally mixed domain.
No algorithm or speedup is promoted without a structured transform and decoder.

proof_obligations.resolution: The exact coset identity and quotient Parseval prove zero/even and inverse-square/odd mass.
Alternating half-interval counting proves T_m(u)<=m/2 for every nonidentity unit.
The range-overlap theorem closes the word-moment bound; positivity transfers it to global-distinct sources.
A mathematical state-weighted near-isometry does not provide coherent access to the dense convolution or its polar factor.
Maximally mixed domain mass is not yet identified with every physical input distribution, and no efficient decoder is compiled.

summary: Closed the all-order four-ray range-overlap lemma and the resulting natural collision-free normalized-Frobenius contraction theorem. The research bottleneck moves from spectral mass to structured dense transform access and physical decoding.

theorem.all_finite_group_range_overlap: Every distinct finite-group pair obeys Tr(P_aP_b)/|G|^2<=3/4; the bound is sharp for C_8 generators a and a^3.
theorem.conditioning_transfer: For S_n, global source distinctness has probability 1-o(1), so E[R|D]<=E[R]/Pr(D)=o(1); Markov gives source-typical contraction.
theorem.different_subgroup_bound: Cauchy on <a> intersect <b> gives |tau(S_a^*S_b)|<=1/3 when the generated cyclic subgroups differ, hence q(a,b)<=2/3.
theorem.equal_subgroup_correlation: For b=a^u, T_m(u)=m-4d_m(u), where d_m(u) counts positive half-circle residues mapped to the negative half-circle.
theorem.half_interval_count: Alternating intervals of length m/(2 min(u,m-u)) prove d_m(u)>=m/8 for every nonidentity unit u.
theorem.natural_frobenius_consequence: The regular word-moment identity now gives E R<=(|G|-1)(3/4)^k, which is o(1) for k=ceil(3log2|G|)+2.
theorem.proper_subgroup_fourier_mass: Parseval gives coefficient mass zero on an even-index subgroup and exactly 1/q^2 on an odd-index subgroup.
theorem.quotient_coset_identity: For m=dq, sum_l s_m(a+ld) is zero for even q and s_d(a) for odd q.
theorem.scope: This proves normalized Frobenius and maximally-mixed-domain spectral tail contraction, not a minimum singular value, physical input domination, structured transform, decoder, or speedup.
